Market today: The mood is cautious, especially for big tech and AI names, with earnings reports from Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft facing skeptical investors after Google's recent sell-off. Macro concerns about El Niño potentially delaying Fed rate cuts could also weigh on growth stocks.

Your holdings: SOXL (-49.65%) and SPAL (-56.9%) are your biggest concerns; both are leveraged ETFs with massive losses and stops that are currently far from the market price. QQQ (-4.55%) and SMH (-13.8%) are also flagged "SELL"/"TRIM" and are nearing their stops. Remember, margin amplifies these drops.

Watch: Keep a very close eye on your QQQ (670) and SMH (540) stops. Also, watch how Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft earnings play out this week, as they'll set the tone for your tech-heavy book.

Bottom line: This is a time for tight risk management and defending your capital, especially with leveraged positions and upcoming tech earnings.
plays: Re-evaluate stops for SOXL and SPAL immediately; their current stops are ineffective given the price action and leverage. Consider trimming if you can't define a new, tighter risk level.
Watch QQQ (670) and SMH (540) stops closely. Be ready to trim if they break, given the broader tech sentiment.
Consider AAPL for a new long if it holds its scanner entry (335.29-334.95) with a stop at 334.2, supported by the iPhone leasing news.
